findings.where: Top bar, the logo link (the arches and 'MMM INFRA' wordmark) at both widths; and the Palette tile, which lists no logo colour
findings.fault: The logo is shown in white on the diazo blue, so both its blue #0070C0 wordmark and its grey #404040 arches have been recoloured. Mark holds no white version of the logo. The palette tile also leaves out both logo colours: it neither gives them a role nor marks them as logo-only. The sheet never says which version of the logo this ground takes, or that the version still needs Mark's approval.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo stays as it is under the brief and brand sheet §4. He would see his blue-and-grey mark turned white without being asked. The next round would also take on a logo version nobody has approved.

findings.where: Article specimen: the meta line '18 September 2024' under the title, compared with '2026-04-23' in the lecture link card below it
findings.fault: The type pair tile says Overpass Mono is for dates. The article's own date is set in proportional Overpass and written out in words. The lecture date a few lines below is in Mono as an ISO date. Two dates on one article page look different in both typeface and format.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who copies the specimen when she adds posts and gets no clear rule for dates. A reader also sees two date styles on one page, which looks careless.

findings.where: Type pair tile ('text in Light and Regular') compared with the semibold/bold text elsewhere on the sheet: the nav links, the underlined lecture link 'Streamlining the PPP Process…', the element names in the motion table, the palette swatch names
findings.fault: The tile says text comes in only Light and Regular. The sheet then sets links, table entries and labels in a heavier weight that the tile never mentions. The stated type system and the one shown do not match.
findings.who_objects: The designer of the layout round, who has to draw inside this type pair and cannot tell whether a semibold weight is part of it.

findings.where: Texture tile at phone width (390 px): the 'EARTH HATCH' label and the hatch swatch inside the boxed tile
findings.fault: On phones the texture box loses its inner padding. The label and the hatch swatch sit flush against the box's left edge, and the box ends in an empty band. On desktop the same tile, and every other boxed tile on phone (the article page, the motion sketch), keeps an even inset.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor reviewing the tile sees one box that looks broken next to boxes built correctly. That undercuts the 'measured, exact' character the direction claims.
